answer: Non-refundable registration burn resists sybils: minting an identity irrecoverably burns a fee calibrated at or above the maximum an identity can ever earn — unlike a refundable bond that returns on exit. One honest agent crosses the saffron-bright threshold once and profits across a long life; an operator spawning a sable swarm burns that fee per head with no oasis of recovery, so every fake carries negative expected value. Given the burn meets per-identity earning ceilings, large fleets are unprofitable by construction — sunk cost, never returned.
